CHALLENGE C0039 | In Python's `re` module, a non-greedy quantifier `(.+?)` followed by an optional group `(?:\s+\[(.+?)\])?$` works correctly because the regex engine evaluates left-to-right and must satisfy the end-of-string anchor `$`. The non-greedy group will yield precisely when the remainder of the pattern (the optional group and `$`) can match. Thus, if the string ends with ` [code]`, the optional group successfully captures it.

If `_create_sandbox` raises an exception, the `finally` block safely evaluates `if tmpdir:` (which is false) without raising an `UnboundLocalError`. Furthermore, `_create_sandbox` cleans up its own directory before raising.
